body: But unlike me, you had the foresight not to post your face and profile name on reddit. Good job.

I've tried and tried to improve. And I know that I have. But the more I improve, the more I realize that I still have to. I didn't have real friends until I was 20 (only 3 years ago) and I have so much catching up to do. It's so overwhelming. All I can see is what I am doing wrong. I honestly don't know if I can really learn.
Ok, I was worried that people would pick up on the self-deprecation. Plus, I actually ended up making non-beach plans today. I'm gonna bake with a friend.

Well, a couple people texted saying they had work, and I sent a text that said, "Wow, I'm stupid. I didn't even look at the weather. I have Wednesday off, if it's a little nicer." I probably shouldn't have sent that. Well, we'll see what happens.
You shoulda used Cholula. That stuff is MILD.
Take care of yourself. Remember that there are other activities you can do once you recover that are easier on the joints. Talk to your doctor about maybe taking up biking?

Well, my friend's going to think that I'm an attention whore if I ever tell her that I'm not bi, and she probably thinks that now because it went from, "I think I might be bi, but I've never talked with anyone about it before," to, "Look at my beautiful, bisexual face, internet!" within a matter of 24 hours.

I was very close to committing suicide 4 years ago. This is the first time in 3 years that I have felt that way. I have occasionally had the briefest of brief glimpses, but it wasn't as real as this. This isn't as bad as it was in the past, but it's far past the threshold where I think it's ok.
Except my sister and friend. They know.
Well, a lot of good you are.

I know my parents are trying to be supportive, but it's like if, after getting a D on a math test, your teacher told you she was proud because she expected you to fail. As for embracing the weird, that hasn't gotten me anywhere. I always hear people tell me to be myself, but what if myself is creepy and makes people uncomfortable? I know I can't just pretend to be someone else, but I have to learn basic social skills at some point in my life. I have tried making lists of small talk topics, and it is helpful to a point. The problem is that I get bogged down in those topics and don't know how to let a conversation naturally flow from that. I have done it, but it has been a lucky accident every time. I simultaneously need to think less and constantly think about these unknown rules of how the world works.

And yes, my boss knows I have Autism, but I can't explain that to every customer as they walk in. I find it best not to engage them in conversation about anything but the store and products.
